title: Environment Setup Overview
overview: Before building React Native applications, you need to install and configure the required development tools. A proper environment setup ensures that you can create, run, debug, and build Android and iOS applications without issues.

example.title: Required Tools
example.content:
Node.js
Java JDK
Android Studio
Android SDK
React Native CLI
Code Editor (VS Code)

title: Installing Node.js
overview: Node.js is required to run JavaScript outside the browser and manage project dependencies. It also installs npm, which is used to install React Native packages and libraries.

title: Installing Java JDK
overview: Java Development Kit (JDK) is required to build Android applications because Gradle uses Java during the build process. Without JDK, Android projects cannot be compiled.

title: Installing Android Studio
overview: Android Studio is the official IDE for Android development. It provides the Android SDK, SDK Manager, Emulator, and build tools required for developing and testing React Native Android applications.

example.title: Components to Install
example.content:
Android SDK
Android SDK Platform
Android SDK Build Tools
Android Emulator
Android Virtual Device (AVD)

title: Setting Environment Variables
overview: Environment variables allow your operating system to locate Java, Android SDK, and platform tools from any terminal window. Correct configuration is necessary for React Native CLI to build Android applications successfully.

title: Creating Your First React Native CLI Project
overview: After installing all required tools, you can create your first React Native CLI project. This command generates the Android and iOS project structure along with all necessary configuration files.

title: Running Your First Application
overview: Once your project is created, start Metro Bundler and launch the application on an Android emulator or a connected physical device. Make sure the emulator is running or USB debugging is enabled on your device.

example.title: Run Commands
example.content:
npx react-native start

npx react-native run-android

title: Topic Summary
overview: You have completed the environment setup for React Native CLI. You learned about the tools required, how to install Node.js, Java JDK, Android Studio, configure environment variables, create your first project, and run it successfully.
